newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen extending gains Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen extending gains Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday eased on profit-taking after a five-session record run, but gains in post-fixing trade signalled another rise on Thursday, analysts said.
They had mixed views on how far the market, which hit a 33-month high on Tuesday, could ride on the wave of this month's revived foreign demand.

"Foreigners have the initiative now so it's hard to point to any technical or fundamental barriers, we have a good mood on world markets and it's spilling over to Poland," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital & Investment.

The main market's all-share WIG index eased 0.3 percent to 15,545.9 points and turnover rose 23 percent to 156.7 million zlotys ($53.8 million) on both markets as a total of 50 issues fell, 19 gained and 19 held flat.

Analysts said the flow of new foreign funds designated to the region with the start of the year, which have centred on blue chip stocks and pushed the market up 10 percent since the new year, could take the WIG to more gains in coming days.
But some said the upside potential was limited by a looming flood of new issues and by big-ticket privatisations expected in the second half of the year.

Analysts saw limited effects of Wednesday's 18.5 percent inflation figure for 1996, as the upbeat market had been largely ignoring macroeconomic signals of late.
They said Tuesday's newcomer Mostostal Krakow leapt 10 percent in speculative trade, helped by the stock's low liquidity.
